title: Do fine-tuned models diverge in SAE feature space? Extending the LoRA feature-geometry study

original_idea.body: Do safety-relevant LoRA fine-tunes diverge in SAE feature space? Extends Feature Geometry of LoRA Adapters (arXiv:2605.28896) using pre-trained SAE + public adapters; rank divergence vs behavioral change.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Detecting unsafe fine-tune drift via feature diffing is a defensible monitoring chain against a concrete misuse scenario.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Pre-trained SAE + public LoRA adapters, inference-only diffing; guided execution feasible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused divergence-ranking deliverable; sourcing safety-relevant adapters adds some dependency.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open-weight monitoring infrastructure, public models, independent-friendly.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference + pre-trained SAE diffing, no training; consumer-GPU feasible.

novelty.reasoning: Extends recent LoRA-SAE study to safety-relevant adapters; angle plausibly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Benign-task version exists; safety-relevant drift angle may be open.
